title: Japan's Anime Market Hits Record $28.2 Billion
paragraphs: Japan's anime industry has reached a new record, thanks largely to fans around the world.

According to early figures from the Association of Japanese Animations (AJA), the country's anime market was worth 4.45 trillion yen, or about $28.2 billion, in 2025. That is 15.8% more than the year before. The figures include not only the anime itself, but also related businesses such as merchandise, music and streaming.

More than half of the money came from outside Japan. Overseas sales reached 2.54 trillion yen, or 57.1% of the total. It was the third year in a row that overseas spending was higher than spending in Japan. However, the domestic market also grew strongly, rising 14.1% to 1.91 trillion yen.
Anime studios themselves also had a record year, earning 505.5 billion yen, an increase of 8.4%. Contracts with overseas companies made up 27.9% of their income, up from 25.5% in 2024.

Big hit movies helped to drive the growth, and many of them were successful far beyond Japan. "Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle" earned nearly $800 million at box offices worldwide, while "Chainsaw Man: Reze Arc" made over $190 million.
Anime is also very popular online. On the movie and TV website IMDb, 100 of the 300 TV series with the most user votes are anime, including nine of the top 20.

Japan hopes the industry will continue to grow in the coming years. The country has set a goal of 6 trillion yen in anime exports, as part of a wider target of 20 trillion yen in overseas content sales by 2033. To reach it, the government plans to support better translation, fight illegal copies and improve distribution.
Kazuhiko Ishikawa, the president of the AJA, said that Japanese animation continues to reach more people around the world.
